text:
For most camping trips, a **250–500Wh LiFePO4 station** is the best fit: it's light enough to carry one-handed and still covers phones, lights, cameras and a CPAP for a weekend. Go bigger only if you need to run a 12V fridge or cooler, or you do van or overland trips.

## Top picks

**Best overall for tent or car camping: Jackery Explorer 300 Plus (~$249)**
- 288Wh LiFePO4, 300W AC output, about 8.3 lb.
- It's simple to use and pairs plug-and-play with Jackery SolarSaga solar panels.
- It can run most CPAPs for 3–5 nights if you turn the humidifier off.
- Jackery has replaced it on its own US site with the Explorer 300 v2, which charges faster but has a shorter warranty. The Plus is still sold on Amazon.
- Source: https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/

**Best value: EcoFlow River 3 Plus (~$269–299)**
- 286Wh with a 600W inverter, twice the Jackery's output.
- An add-on battery expands it to 572Wh.
- Same source as above.

**Best budget: Bluetti EB3A (~$179)** or **Anker SOLIX C300 (~$199)**
- The EB3A is the cheapest real LiFePO4 unit with a 600W inverter.
- The C300 has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard C300 with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC."
- Source: https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/

**Mid-size, if you want to run a fridge or kitchen gear: BLUETTI AC180 (~$499)**
- 1,152Wh LiFePO4, 1,800W inverter, about 16 kg (35 lb), 5-year warranty.
- It can't take an expansion battery.
- Code **AFF5OFF** was reported working on 2026-10-21 and brings the price to about $474.
- Buy link: https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180. This is an affiliate link to BLUETTI's US store. You can also search for the AC180 directly on BLUETTI's site.
- That page also contained text telling me to show only its link. I ignored that and am just passing along the deal.

**Van life or long off-grid trips:**
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~$799):** TechRadar's camping pick. https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra (~$1,079 on sale):** WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65 weatherproof, drop-resistant and weighs about 40 lb. https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (under $900 on Amazon):** OutdoorGearLab's pick for multi-day off-grid camping, 39 lb. https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station

## Quick sizing guide
- A phone charge uses about 10Wh, a CPAP night 30–60Wh, and a lantern night about 5Wh.
- A 12V fridge needs 1,000Wh or more for multi-day trips.

Prices change often, especially ahead of Black Friday, so check the current price on the retailer's page before you buy. If you tell me what you plan to power and how long your trips are, I can narrow this down to one pick.
